title.en: Phrases that hold a meeting together

es: Reconocer las frases que sirven para abrir, opinar, interrumpir, aclarar, resumir y cerrar una reunión, y su nivel de cortesía.

teaching.en: Let's start the meeting. Today we need a name for the club.
teaching.es: Empecemos la reunión. Hoy necesitamos un nombre para el club.
teaching.explanationEs: Let's start abre la reunión: es la frase habitual de quien dirige.
segments: Let's start the meeting. Today we
need a name for the club.
teaching.audioText: Let's start the meeting. Today we need a name for the club.

teaching.en: In my opinion, a short name is better.
teaching.es: En mi opinión, un nombre corto es mejor.
teaching.explanationEs: In my opinion + frase completa: das tu opinión de forma educada.
teaching.audioText: In my opinion, a short name is better.

teaching.en: Sorry to interrupt, but I have a question.
teaching.es: Perdona que te interrumpa, pero tengo una pregunta.
teaching.explanationEs: Sorry to interrupt, but… es la fórmula cortés para hablar en medio de otra persona.
teaching.audioText: Sorry to interrupt, but I have a question.

teaching.en: Could you explain that again, please?
teaching.es: ¿Podrías explicarlo otra vez, por favor?
teaching.explanationEs: Could you…? pide una aclaración con cortesía; es más suave que «Explain that».
teaching.audioText: Could you explain that again, please?

teaching.en: To sum up, everyone wants a short name for the club.
teaching.es: En resumen, todos quieren un nombre corto para el club.
teaching.explanationEs: To sum up + frase: resume lo decidido antes de cerrar.
segments: To sum up, everyone wants a
teaching.audioText: To sum up, everyone wants a short name for the club.

teaching.en: That is all for today. Thanks, everyone.
teaching.es: Eso es todo por hoy. Gracias a todos.
teaching.explanationEs: That is all for today cierra la reunión; thanks, everyone da las gracias.
teaching.audioText: That is all for today. Thanks, everyone.

To sum up, we need a new poster.

hint.es: Empieza con la expresión que introduce tu opinión.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de reunión con su función.

es: Hacer sugerencias con how about + -ing, why don't we y let's, y discrepar con cortesía ofreciendo una alternativa.

teaching.en: How about making a poster for the picnic?

teaching.en: Why don't we have the picnic on Sunday?

teaching.en: Eight members attended the meeting on 12 May.

teaching.explanationEs: Attended + reunión (sin to): la primera parte del acta dice quién estuvo.

teaching.en: First, we discussed the plan for the school fair.
teaching.es: Primero, hablamos del plan para la feria de la escuela.

teaching.en: Then we decided to hold the fair on 20 June.

teaching.explanationEs: Then / after that + decided to: las decisiones se cuentan en pasado.

teaching.en: Finally, Sara will send the posters by 5 June.

answer.text: Minutes of the volunteer club meeting, 12 May. Eight members attended the meeting. First, we discussed the beach. Then we decided to clean the beach on Saturday 23 May and to buy gloves and bags. After that, we agreed on the tasks, and each task has a deadline. Tom will buy the gloves by 20 May. Mia will ask the council for permission by 15 May. Finally, we agreed to meet again on 19 May to check the plan. Everyone is responsible for one task.

Club meeting, 12 May. Eight members attended. First, we discussed how to clean the beach. Then we decided to clean it on Saturday 23 May. After that, we decided to buy gloves and bags. teaching.en: Welcome, everyone. Today I will lead the meeting.

prompt.es: Escribe lo que dices al dirigir la reunión de teatro (90–120 palabras).

answer.text: Welcome, everyone. Today I will lead the meeting. We need to choose a day for the play. Leo, it is your turn. What is your idea? Leo says, how about Friday? Mia, go ahead. I see your point, Leo, but I am not sure about Friday because we have a test. Does anyone have another idea? Why don't we have the play on Saturday? Everyone agreed. To sum up, Leo will make the tickets by Wednesday, and Mia will ask for the hall by Tuesday. That is all for today. Thanks, everyone.
accepted: Welcome, everyone. Today I will lead the meeting. We need to choose a day for the play. Leo, it is your turn. What is your idea? Leo says, how about Friday? Mia, go ahead. I see your point, Leo, but I am not sure about Friday because we have a test. Does anyone have another idea? Why don't we have the play on Saturday? Everyone agreed. To sum up, Leo will make the tickets by Wednesday, and Mia will ask for the hall by Tuesday. That is all for today. Thanks, everyone.

Welcome, everyone. Let's start the meeting. We need a day for the play. Leo, it is your turn. Leo thinks Friday is a good day, but Mia is not sure because she has a test on Friday. Does anyone have another idea? How about Saturday instead? We agreed on Saturday. To sum up, Leo will make the tickets by Wednesday, and Mia will book the hall by Tuesday. That is all for today. Thank you for coming.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta abre la reunión, da turnos, discrepa con cortesía, resume tareas con will y by, y cierra.

origin.text: Diriges la reunión del club de teatro para elegir el día de la función. Leo propone el viernes; Mia duda porque hay un examen; alternativa: el sábado. Decisión: sábado. Tareas: Leo hace las entradas (hasta el miércoles) y Mia pide la sala (hasta el martes). Abre, da la palabra, discrepa con cortesía, resume y cierra.
